meta.title: What Kind of Learner Driver Are You?
meta.hook: Three quick sections. One driver type. Zero judgment.
meta.audience: For learner drivers (and the people teaching them)

sections.blurb: How your hazard radar and road smarts are shaping up.

sections.label: Brain Behind the Wheel

sections.subtitle: Section 3 of 3
sections.blurb: How you take in the sights, sounds and motion of driving.

questions.text: A ball bounces onto the road ahead. Before you even spot a kid, what are you already doing?

options.text: Easing off and covering the brake — where there's a ball, there's usually a kid.
Slowing a little and scanning the footpaths.
Keeping on, but watching more closely now.
Honestly? I'd probably notice the kid, not the ball.

questions.text: You and the 3-second following gap are…

options.text: Best mates — I actually count it out.
Comfortable — I leave a good gap without thinking.
Trying — but in traffic it shrinks on me.
Gap? I like to keep things moving.

questions.text: A light's been green a while as you approach (a 'stale' green). You…

options.text: Ease off — it could change, and I've already planned my stop.
Check mirrors and get ready for either outcome.
Keep at the limit, ready to brake.
Nudge the speed up to make it through.

questions.text: Your honest take on road rules?

options.text: They're the shared code that keeps everyone safe — I'm all in.
Mostly sensible; I follow them and think about why.
Still learning which ones matter most in the moment.
Some feel more like suggestions when the road's empty.

questions.text: It starts bucketing rain on a road you don't know. Your move?

options.text: Slow down, bigger gap, lights on, both hands, full focus.
Ease off and drive to the conditions.
Grip the wheel and concentrate really hard.
Same speed — I trust the car.

questions.text: Your supervisor says: 'Next left, then second right, pull over past the servo.' You…

options.text: Repeat it back and picture the route — locked in.
Get the first bit and ask about the rest as I go.
Remember 'left' and hope the rest comes back to me.
Wait — was it second right, or right at the second one?

questions.text: Your favourite song comes on mid-roundabout. What happens to your driving?

options.text: Barely notice it — the roundabout has all of me.
I enjoy it but stay on task.
Split focus for a second, then re-centre.
I might vibe out for a moment.

questions.text: Plans change: your usual route is closed and you're detoured somewhere new. You feel…

options.text: Fine — I adapt and re-plan on the fly.
A bit thrown, but I settle quickly.
Stressed — I really like knowing the plan.
Overloaded — new and unexpected at once is a lot.

questions.text: How do you go with catching your own mistakes while driving?

options.text: Straight away — I'm always quietly self-checking.
Usually catch them and learn from them.
Sometimes need my supervisor to point them out.
Often don't clock them until afterwards.

questions.text: Before you even turn the key, you…

options.text: Seat, mirrors, belt, phone away, plan the trip — full ritual.
Do the basics and set off.
Adjust things as I remember them.
Just go — I'll sort it as I drive.

questions.text: Your ideal vibe inside the car is…

options.text: Quiet and calm — no radio, minimal chat, just the road.
Low background music, comfy temperature.
Music up, energy on, let's go.
I don't really notice the cabin either way.

questions.text: Oncoming headlights at night, harsh glare, or low sun in your eyes…

options.text: Really get to me — I squint, tense up, want to slow right down.
Mildly annoying; I adjust and carry on.
Barely register them.
Love night driving — lights everywhere, bring it on.

questions.text: On a long, boring stretch of highway, you…

options.text: Get restless and crave something happening.
Find it relaxing and easy.
Have to work to stay alert — easy to zone out.
Notice every little sound and sensation in the car.

questions.text: Busy intersection — pedestrians, noise, several lanes, someone talking to you. You feel…

options.text: Overwhelmed — too much coming in at once.
Focused but fine; I filter it out.
Energised — I like a busy scene.
I mostly tune the extra stuff out (maybe a bit too much).

questions.text: How well do you notice when your body needs something (tired, hungry, a break) while driving?

options.text: Immediately — I feel it clearly, and it can distract me.
Pretty well; I plan my breaks.
Not until it's a big deal.
I'd rather just push on and keep driving.
